panels.title: Live Trading Signals
panels.description: Actionable direct notifications are PRE-A0 and A0 only. A1/A2 remain visible below as diagnostic engine state but are not sent to Slack.

panels.title: Active Trading Signals
panels.description: Number of currently active realtime breakout signals (A0 strongest + A1 confirmed + A2 early-warning) the engine snapshot is reporting.

panels.title: A0 — Slack Action Tier
panels.description: Active confirmed A0 breakouts. A0 is pushed directly by the realtime producer to the Slack main feed; A1 and A2 are deliberately excluded from Slack.

panels.title: Watched Symbols
panels.description: How many symbols the realtime engine is actively polling for breakout signals.

panels.title: Signals Snapshot Age
panels.description: Seconds since the realtime engine last wrote latest_realtime_signals.json. Red once the snapshot is older than the 480s (8 min) max signal age — stale signals should not be trusted. Shows N/A when the snapshot timestamp is unknown.

panels.title: External Consumer Watchdog
panels.description: Whether this deployment expects an external client to call /smc_live during the US regular market session. NO CONSUMER EXPECTED is the correct current state; CONSUMER EXPECTED arms missing-traffic alerts after a verified client rollout.

panels.title: PRE-A0 Alerts — Last Hour
panels.description: Direct PRE-A0 Slack dispatches during the last hour. PRE-A0 is unconfirmed and appears only after offline + shadow gates, calibration, explicit deployment approval, deduplication and the hourly budget all pass.

panels.title: How to read & export this section
panels.description: Static help: interpreting an empty table and exporting the signal panels to Excel/CSV.

options.content:
**Slack routing:** only direct PRE-A0 and A0 notifications go to the main feed; A1/A2 stay dashboard-only. **No rows?** Signal panels contain rows only while active A0, A1, or A2 signals exist, usually during US trading hours. Empty means there are currently no live signals; it is not an error. Confirm source health with **Active Trading Signals** (zero means quiet) and **Signals Snapshot Age** (low means fresh).  
**Export to Excel:** panel menu → **Inspect → Data → Download CSV**.

panels.title: Signal Strength - Live Ranking (now)
panels.description: At-a-glance ranking of every active signal right now: one horizontal bar per symbol, coloured by score (grey <1, blue 1-5, green >=5). The big, readable snapshot - for history use the trend chart below, for detail the table. Empty = no active signals right now.

panels.title: Signal Score — Active Symbols
panels.description: Trend of each active signal's ranking score over time - see which symbols are strengthening or fading. Full-width plot (legend moved below so the chart uses the whole width). For the at-a-glance 'now' view use the bar gauge above; for per-symbol detail use the table.

panels.title: Top Trading Signals — Latest Detail
panels.description: Per-symbol detail of the active breakout signals (sorted by ranking score, highest first). Level: A0 = strongest confirmed breakout, A1 = confirmed, A2 = early-warning (unconfirmed, building momentum). Direction is the trade bias; Score is the engine's v2 ranking; Tech is the 0-1 technical score; Change % is the intraday move; Freshness decays 1->0 as the signal ages. Empty = no active signals right now (rows only exist while breakouts fire) - not an error. Export: panel menu -> Inspect -> Data -> Download CSV (opens in Excel).

panels.title: Daily Signal Experiment
panels.description: Daily forward-test results by signal family and timeframe, including hit rate, sample size, and history.

panels.title: Daily Experiment — Snapshot Age
panels.description: Age of the latest Plan 2.8 family rollup (scripts/plan_2_8_tf_family_rollup.py). The rolling benchmark runs Mon-Fri; green < 72h, yellow < 96h, red beyond 96h — the daemon's OVERLAY_EXPERIMENT_MAX_AGE_SECS staleness budget, where lo-experiment-snapshot-stale fires — means a run was skipped (Friday's rollup is legitimately ~89.5h old by Monday). N/A when the run date cannot be derived.

panels.title: Daily Experiment — Files Scanned
panels.description: Number of scoring files folded into the latest daily rollup. A sudden drop signals an upstream scoring/coverage problem.

panels.title: FVG 5m Verdict (Phase E2)
panels.description: Latest Phase E2 verdict for the FVG-time-to-fill 5m hypothesis vs baseline. measured = conclusive signal; underpowered = effect seen but not enough samples; insufficient/missing = not enough data yet.

panels.title: BOS 4H Verdict (Phase E2)
panels.description: Latest Phase E2 verdict for the BOS 4H stability hypothesis vs baseline.

panels.title: Daily Experiment — Latest Per-Family Detail
panels.description: Current-day hit-rate and sample size for each SMC setup family (BOS / OB / FVG / SWEEP) per timeframe, from the latest rollup. Hit-rate is colour-graded; n_events is the sample size behind it.

panels.title: Family Hit-Rate Over Time (accumulates daily)
panels.description: Live forward timeline: each daily benchmark run updates these gauges, so Prometheus records one step per day. Use the time picker (e.g. last 30 days) to see how each family/timeframe hit-rate trends going forward.

panels.title: Per-Day Family Hit-Rate — History (backfilled)
panels.description: Retained per-day history from plan_2_8_history.jsonl: exact hit-rate and sample size for each run date / timeframe / family. Backfills the daily statistics immediately (no need to wait for Prometheus to accumulate). Sort by Run Date to read the day-by-day timeline.

panels.title: Sweep-Trap Promotion Evidence
panels.description: Observe-only evaluation of the sweep-trap detector. The daily workflow measures prediction quality on the latest rolling corpus and stores one evidence row per run. The detector still has no scoring weight; promotion requires a separate decision.

panels.title: Sweep-Trap Shadow Verdict
panels.description: Latest evaluation state. INCONCLUSIVE means fewer than 40 pooled shadow samples. SHADOW means the sample floor is met but prediction quality fails at least one gate. PROMOTABLE means Brier score improves and tercile lift is positive; it is a candidate for review, not out-of-sample validation or automatic activation.

panels.title: Shadow Brier Delta
panels.description: baseline_brier - signal_brier on the shadow corpus. Positive = the sweep_trap_quality_score adds predictive skill over the no-score baseline; <= 0 = no skill (stays in shadow).

panels.title: Shadow Tercile Lift
panels.description: Top-tercile minus bottom-tercile reversal hit-rate by sweep_trap_quality_score (computed only when each tercile has >= 6 samples). Positive = the score discriminates good setups from bad; 0 when underpowered.

panels.title: Samples in Latest Evaluation
panels.description: Valid sweep samples in the latest rolling evaluation corpus. This number can rise or fall when the corpus changes; the evidence ledger accumulates daily rows separately. At least 40 pooled shadow samples are required before a verdict can leave INCONCLUSIVE.

panels.title: Shadow Snapshot Age
panels.description: Age of the latest shadow-eval snapshot. The workflow runs Mon-Fri; green < 72h, yellow < 96h, red beyond 96h (the OVERLAY_SWEEP_TRAP_SHADOW_MAX_AGE_SECS budget where lo-sweep-trap-shadow-stale fires). N/A when the age is unknown.

panels.title: Latest Sweep-Trap Evidence
panels.description: Decision table for the newest rolling-corpus evaluation. Date is the corpus date, not the dashboard refresh time. A promotable candidate needs at least 40 valid samples, a positive Brier delta, and positive tercile lift. This table is informational and does not activate the detector.
